Not only have they contributed to it, but they understand first hand the benefits and the drawbacks. They know life without the advancements that exist today.   📞Take the ti
comment_text: So, Yonkers lets help our seniors by helping them sell their homes without a delay from City on closing out old permits. It seems what is happening to my mother, is a problem all over the City with permits from decades ago not being closed. There must have been a situation back then that created this situation. The process involving my Mother's home is taking too long (months) and we finally got inspections but I have not heard about whether I can send in the last paper to finally close these permits. It is not just the money but the aggravation and time it takes so selling a home is often delayed and buyers walk away. My mother who is 90 has now two neighbors who encroached on her property and did so without permits. But, what does the City do now? Nada. Where is the fairness in that. My mother lived in Yonkers 67 years but because she fell and her medical alert button did not work, she ended up in a nursing home for 5 months. She did not break anything but the hospitalization during Covid made her condition worse to live in a house with lots of steps up the front. Truly, Yonkers if you really cared about your Seniors, help them by fixing your Housing and Building issues.
author: Sandra Harrison
